prompt: What distinguishes `git clone` from forking on GitHub?
explanation: They answer different needs: clone = get the code onto your machine; fork = get a copy onto GitHub under your account so pull requests back to the original are possible. Contribution typically does both.

options.text: Clone gives you a local working copy; a fork gives you a GitHub-hosted copy you can propose changes from
Clone and fork are two commands for the same thing
Cloning requires write access; forking does not
A fork is local; a clone is on GitHub
